notes: The breadboard image labels the upper half rows j-f and the lower half rows e-a, while the catalogue puts rows a-e in bank 't' and f-j in bank 'b'. I followed the row letters: the upper half is bank 'b' and the lower half is bank 't'. Rails are named by position in the image: 'tp' and 'tn' are the top + and - rails, and 'bp' and 'bn' are the bottom + and - rails.
Rail hole numbers (tp.1, tn.2, tp.4, tn.8, tn.24, tp.25, bp.3, bp.10, bn.5, bn.13, bn.24, bp.25) are estimates from the picture. Only which rail each part uses matters electrically.
The pushbutton straddles the centre gap. Its left legs sit in column 5 and its right legs in column 7. Column 5 carries 5V (side 1) and column 7 carries pin 2 plus the pull-down resistor (side 2).

The two analog sensors are drawn as FSRs. Each has one lead in the + rail and the other in a column that goes to an analog pin and to a 10k resistor to the - rail. The sensor in column 6 goes to A1 (inner yellow wire) and the sensor in column 16 goes to A0 (outer yellow wire), as in the image.
The three 10k resistors are given value=10000. The black wire from the Uno goes to the second GND pin, GND.2.
The long black and red wires on the right join the top rails to the bottom rails, so the bottom rails are powered too.
